entities.summary:
Vasugupta (fl. late 8th to early 9th century CE, died 925 CE) was a pivotal philosopher and yogi from Kashmir, whose seminal work, the *Shiva Sutras*, laid the foundational scriptural basis for the nondual spiritual tradition of Kashmir Shaivism, also known as Trika. Emerging during a vibrant period of intellectual and religious synthesis in the Indian subcontinent, Vasugupta's teachings offered a radical reinterpretation of Shaiva philosophy, asserting the inherent divinity within each individual and the world itself. His work articulated a direct path to liberation through recognition (*pratyabhijna*), significantly influencing subsequent generations of spiritual masters and shaping the religious landscape of medieval Kashmir.

The *Shiva Sutras*, a collection of 77 aphorisms, is traditionally said to have been revealed to Vasugupta by Shiva himself, either through a dream or inscribed on a rock on Mount Mahadeva in the Harwan region near Srinagar. This mystical origin story underscores the text's profound authority within the tradition. Vasugupta subsequently compiled and perhaps systematized these cryptic verses, which elucidate the nature of consciousness, the cosmos as a manifestation of divine will, and practical methods for spiritual realization. His direct disciples, such as Kallata and Somananda, were instrumental in transmitting and commenting upon these sutras, ensuring their survival and interpretation for future generations.
